# Parallelization with Python

<p class="when">{{< var event.date >}}, {{< var event.time >}} · {{< var event.where >}}</p>

Use more of your computer's cores to get the same work done sooner.
:::

## What we'll do

- Learn the types of parallelization and where your own work fits.
- Spread an "embarrassingly parallel" task across cores with Python's `multiprocessing`.
- Time it across core counts to see where the gains level off.
- See a case where parallel is slower, and why.

## Get the notebook

- **Google Colab, nothing to install:** open the [learner notebook in Colab]({{< var colab.learner >}}), click
  **Copy to Drive**, and run the two **Setup** cells.
- **JupyterLab on your laptop, all your cores:** follow the [Setup](setup.qmd) steps, about 15 minutes.

The [filled notebook]({{< var colab.filled >}}) has every answer. Follow along in the [slides](slides/index.qmd).
